cells.tense: Right now you are standing at the start of something you mean to build.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Pick a concrete thing someone near you needs, do it now, and see it through to done.
cells.core:
Right now you are holding the first piece of something you mean to build, and it is doing what a first piece should: it is turning into the rest. When a start lands well, the made thing gets made and the next move is obvious by itself. You are working on one of those and there is no need to look past it.

A concrete hand offered to someone near you, taken all the way to finished in one sitting, keeps the line moving. Not a sweeping gesture — enough to close before the tea goes cold. That is what makes a beginning readable: someone else can see it, and so can you, and neither of you has to call it anything.
cells.sheetLine: A finished thing makes the next one obvious.
cells.verb: starting the first piece of what will be built

cells.tense: You are pushing for a completion that cannot be imagined from here.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Take a page, name every feeling this one has stirred, and leave every one of them standing.
cells.core:
You are pushing something toward a finished shape that cannot be imagined from here, and the pushing runs ahead of anything you have. There is nothing to brace against yet — the next step has no picture, and it cannot be forced into one. Hoping harder will not get it.

Before the next move, put every feeling about this onto one page, all of them, none crossed out. It will not fit a theme and it will not be tidy. Stay with the page until the whole of it is legible, and the push will have somewhere to stand. What is actually complete can be measured against it rather than guessed at.
cells.sheetLine: You are forcing a shape the thing cannot wear yet.
cells.verb: starting the first piece of what will be built

cells.tense: You were standing at the start of something, and the starting has gone quiet.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Put all of it out where it can be taken in at once, and stay with it until no piece is left turned away.
cells.core:
A first piece of something was there, and it has gone quiet. What you meant to build lives as a heap in a back room — all still sitting, none of it started, and you in front of it half turned away. The pull toward it is still in you. It is not doing anything right now.

Put the pieces where they can be taken in together — no cupboard, no stack, everything in view. Stay with them until no piece is left turned away, and start nothing. What is whole there is already yours to take in; that alone is the first cut of a beginning, and it will not need pushing from you.
cells.sheetLine: You want it built, and nothing has been started.
cells.verb: starting the first piece of what will be built

cells.tense: The pen is already moving on this building, with your hand not claiming it.
cells.act: see the true thing whole, as the last word on it
cells.ask: Look at one finished piece already on the table until you can take it in whole, and take it as yours.
cells.core:
The pen is already moving on this building, and you talk about it as if nothing is happening. You are making small finished pieces and calling them luck, or saying anyone would have. The pieces are on the table — the concrete bit is real. The maker part of the work is the part you have not put your name to.

Take one finished thing that is already done, and look at it until you can see all of it at once — what it took, what it's made of, that it stands. No credit to argue for. Holding it whole, with no doorway left to hide behind, is how a beginning gets kept, and you will need it kept for the next one.
cells.sheetLine: The building is already underway in your name.
cells.verb: starting the first piece of what will be built
